topic: For i.i.d. O=(L0,A0,L1,A1,Y), binary treatments, bounded outcomes, overlap, and the fixed regime (1,1), impose Tan-compatible sequential propensity-ratio normalizations and Zhang--Zhao marginal-history second-moment budgets. Prove that the compatible-full-law counterfactual-mean set is a compact interval exactly equal to the convex perspective program in w1=h1 and w0=h0h1, that conditional projection restores the required h0(L0,Y) factorization, and that both endpoints have compatible attaining full laws. Derive the exact two-global-price conditional clipped-affine root dual, including zero-price and unit-budget faces. On compact regular budget regions construct cross-fitted one-step endpoint processes with a joint uniform Gaussian multiplier band; extend bands by the deterministic outcome range and monotonicity to obtain honest full-calibration-ray breakdown inversion at ties, flat crossings, and absent crossings, without claiming shrinking Gaussian inference on excluded faces or inference for learned dynamic regimes. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Conditional projection preserves the objective and normalizations while lowering the perspective budget, L^(4/3) by L2 compactness yields attainment, the corrected finite grid has regular primal-dual gaps at most 6.4e-13 and inactive-face certificates at most 5e-16, and optimized-value derivative checks support an influence function with both propensity-floor corrections. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the uniform quadratic held-out mean-bias bound, score continuity, and conditional-root operator stability for the explicit cross-fitted influence function, including both propensity floors and the global-price/root perturbations. EARLY KILL TEST: On the specified finite two-baseline, two-intermediate-history, three-outcome law with active clipping at both stages, independently perturb every observed-law component and compare certified constrained-value derivatives with influence-function covariances, then jointly perturb nuisances and prices; any reproducible derivative mismatch or linear held-out bias kills the inference spine. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_seqavg_waterfill_inference.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For two-period binary treatment and a fixed regime, characterize the sharp compatible-full-law bounds on the counterfactual mean under sequential propensity-ratio normalizations and global second-moment budgets, including an exact finite-dimensional dual on active and inactive budget faces.

source_refs.claim: The paper solves the cross-sectional second-moment propensity-ratio model and explicitly leaves extension of the average-case model to observational studies over time open.
source_refs.author: Yao Zhang and Qingyuan Zhao

source_refs.claim: Tan derives population sharp and conservative convex representations for sequential sensitivity models with range-bounded ratios while leaving specialized computation and sample sensitivity analysis unresolved.
source_refs.author: Zhiqiang Tan

source_refs.claim: This work treats static or time-varying treatments and gives estimators for longitudinal sensitivity bounds, but under sensitivity constructions distinct from Tan's fully normalized sharp model.
source_refs.author: Matteo Bonvini, Edward H. Kennedy, Valerie Ventura, and Larry Wasserman

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zhang and Zhao's sharp clipped-affine optimizer is cross-sectional: its mean-one constraint is conditional on one baseline history and its second-moment constraint has one global price. In a two-period full law, the early distortion enters through a product weight while late and early normalizations live on different histories. Tan supplies sequential full-law bookkeeping for range-bounded ratios but not an average-case quadratic budget. The first proof step that changes is the reduction from latent full laws to observed-law weights: conditional projection must preserve the objective and both normalizations while lowering the perspective budget, after which one must reconstruct an attaining full law. No located paper combines Tan-compatible sequential normalization with Zhang–Zhao second-moment budgets.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem proving that the compatible counterfactual-mean set is a compact interval equal to a convex perspective program, with compatible endpoint-attaining full laws and a strong-duality formula whose two global prices yield conditional clipped-affine root equations, including zero-price and unit-budget cases.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from the pessimism of worst-case sensitivity parameters to an interpretable second-moment budget, then land on its explicitly stated longitudinal extension.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Worst-case propensity-ratio caps can be driven by rare extremes -> second-moment budgets measure average confounding strength and permit sharper calibration -> longitudinal treatment introduces history-specific normalization and product weights -> derive the exact sharp compatible sequential program.

method_exemplars.technique: Sequential density-ratio reparameterization, normalization constraints, convex bound representations, and constructive full-data distributions attaining sharp bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the same two-period full-law compatibility problem for range-bounded ratios; the new proof must replace its box constraints by marginal-history quadratic perspective constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Lagrangian solution of a propensity-ratio second-moment program via conditional clipped-affine weights and a global multiplier/root characterization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its cross-sectional optimizer is the direct donor for each sequential conditional subproblem, while the destination requires coupled prices and a product-weight perspective.

method_exemplars.technique: Distributionally robust sharp-bound representation followed by efficient influence-function construction and doubly sharp/doubly valid endpoint estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how a sharp marginal-sensitivity optimization can be converted into an estimable endpoint with limit theory, providing the nearest inference rung once the sequential quadratic endpoint is identified.

open_problems.open_problem: Under which primitive nuisance-learner norms, rates, and margin conditions do cross-fitted one-step estimators of sequential second-moment sensitivity endpoints achieve uniformly quadratic held-out mean bias when both propensity floors, global prices, and conditional roots are estimated?

source_refs.claim: Tan's longitudinal analysis is population-level and states that estimation of the ICE/IPW functionals and doubly or multiply robust sample procedures remain to be developed.
source_refs.author: Zhiqiang Tan

source_refs.claim: For one treatment, Zhang and Zhao derive efficient one-step estimators and multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous bands for second-moment sensitivity curves.
source_refs.author: Yao Zhang and Qingyuan Zhao

source_refs.claim: The paper gives efficient estimators and confidence intervals for several marginal-structural-model sensitivity bounds with time-varying treatment, establishing an adjacent but differently constrained longitudinal inference result.
source_refs.author: Matteo Bonvini, Edward H. Kennedy, Valerie Ventura, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.excerpt: The load-bearing O_P(a_K) total-variation bound is an estimator-side restriction

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature splits along the relevant boundary: Zhang and Zhao provide one-step and uniform-band theory for a sharp one-treatment second-moment endpoint, Tan provides compatible sequential population sharpness but not inference, and Bonvini et al. provide longitudinal inference for differently constrained bounds. The prior reviewer artifact identifies the analogous danger of assuming a high-level estimator-side variation bound merely to force a product-rate remainder. Here an observed-law perturbation changes two propensities, both clipping floors, nested conditional regressions, two global multipliers, and conditional roots. The missing proof must replace an assumed high-level remainder by a conditional root-map expansion that derives score continuity, price/root stability, and quadratic held-out bias from primitive learner rates and clipping-margin conditions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition and uniform asymptotic-linearity theorem for the joint lower/upper cross-fitted one-step process, deriving an o_p(n^-1/2) held-out mean-bias bound from explicit nuisance norms and rates, with an influence function containing both propensity-floor and price/root terms and a valid joint Gaussian multiplier band on compact regular budget regions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its discussion isolates sample sensitivity analysis as the next step immediately after establishing sequential population bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sequential unconfoundedness is untestable -> compatible population bounds quantify departures -> practical use requires estimating the nested endpoint -> sharp average-case endpoints require cross-fitted uniform inference with every optimizer perturbation included.

method_exemplars.technique: Envelope-based efficient influence-function derivation for an optimized second-moment bound, cross-fitted one-step correction, and multiplier bootstrap for a sensitivity-indexed process.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact single-stage estimator-and-band template; the resolution must establish that its envelope calculation survives sequential product weights and two coupled optimizer equations.

method_exemplars.technique: Longitudinal efficient influence-function recursion for sensitivity bounds with static or time-varying treatments and flexible nuisance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest donor for the sequential nuisance recursion and held-out remainder decomposition, although the target endpoint has sharper normalization and a different optimizer.

method_exemplars.technique: Neyman-orthogonal scores, sample splitting, cross-fitting, and product-rate control of nuisance-induced remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem must turn the sequential endpoint score into an orthogonal moment and reduce held-out bias to products of nuisance and root/price errors.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct honest confidence sets for the entire calibration-ray breakdown region by inverting sequential second-moment endpoint bands when crossings are tied, flat, or absent and the ray includes nonregular zero-price or unit-budget faces?

source_refs.author: Matthew A. Masten and Alexandre Poirier

source_refs.claim: Zhang and Zhao construct multiplier bands for cross-sectional average-case sensitivity curves but do not develop longitudinal calibration-ray breakdown inversion.
source_refs.author: Yao Zhang and Qingyuan Zhao

source_refs.excerpt: supplies neither uniform anti-concentration nor an observable common-multiplier coupling through variance degeneracy

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing sensitivity papers supply bands for endpoint or frontier curves, while inverse-set work supplies a general deterministic inversion principle; the located literature does not combine these for a sequential average-case sensitivity ray. Direct inverse-function arguments fail at ties, flat contacts, and missing crossings, while Gaussian endpoint expansions degenerate on unit-budget or zero-price faces. The prior CausalSmith obligation adds a concrete implementation barrier: population Gaussianization alone supplies neither observable common-multiplier coupling nor uniform anti-concentration through variance degeneracy. The first proof step must therefore define breakdown as a set-valued inverse of a simultaneously covered joint endpoint process and extend coverage to excluded faces using the known outcome range and population monotonicity, rather than extrapolating a shrinking Gaussian approximation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving a feasible common-multiplier band on compact regular budget regions and deterministic inner and outer confidence sets for the full calibration-ray breakdown region, with honest coverage under unique crossings, ties, flat crossings, absent crossings, variance degeneracy, and range-based extension across excluded faces.

writing_exemplar.why: Adopt its reversal from estimating effects under assumptions to asking for the weakest assumptions sustaining a conclusion, while replacing its one-period frontier by a sequential calibration ray.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A sensitivity curve reports conclusions under many assumptions -> users want the weakest budget sustaining a claim -> this is an inverse-set object rather than an ordinary endpoint -> honest reporting must remain defined at flat, tied, boundary, and absent crossings.

method_exemplars.technique: Deterministic inversion of simultaneous confidence bands into inner and outer confidence sets for function preimages, with simultaneous multi-threshold coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A breakdown ray is the preimage of a conclusion set under a monotone endpoint function; band inversion avoids requiring a unique nonzero-slope root.

method_exemplars.technique: Directional delta methods and derivative-aware resampling for nondifferentiable functionals, together with a proof that the standard bootstrap generally fails without full differentiability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Ties and min/max truncations make frontier and generalized-inverse maps only directionally differentiable, explaining the nonregular cases that deterministic band inversion must protect.

method_exemplars.technique: Multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous confidence bands for an entire second-moment sensitivity curve.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the band to invert on regular budget regions; the new work is the sequential joint band and honest non-Gaussian extension to the full ray.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the jointly attainable vector of counterfactual means for several fixed longitudinal regimes under one common full law and shared sequential second-moment budgets, and determine when coordinatewise sharp endpoints are simultaneously attainable.

source_refs.author: Yao Zhang and Qingyuan Zhao

open_problems.why_unsolved: Coordinatewise optimization can choose a different latent law for each regime and therefore does not determine whether an ATE, policy contrast, or collection of regime means is compatible with one common data-generating law. Tan shows that this distinction already matters for sequential range-bounded models under stronger cross-regime consistency. With second-moment budgets, shared latent propensities and counterfactual intermediate covariates couple regime-specific product weights quadratically. The first proof step that changes from a single-regime construction is the full-law gluing argument: it must preserve every regime-specific consistency identity and all shared budgets simultaneously. No located paper gives a joint-set or simultaneous-attainment result for longitudinal average-case propensity-ratio sensitivity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A support-function or convex-program characterization of the joint identified set of a finite vector of fixed-regime means, with necessary and sufficient conditions for simultaneous coordinatewise attainment and either an explicit compatible-full-law construction or a sharp counterexample regime.

writing_exemplar.why: Its multiple-strategy discussion cleanly frames why coordinatewise sharpness and simultaneous full-law attainability are different questions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Applied contrasts compare several treatment paths -> separate sharp bounds may use incompatible latent laws -> sequential consistency couples counterfactual histories -> characterize the common-law joint set under average-case budgets.

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-regime extension of sequential density ratios and constructive simultaneous-attainment arguments under explicit consistency conventions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It identifies the precise gluing issue that the second-moment joint-set proof must resolve.

method_exemplars.technique: Quadratic propensity-ratio budgets, convex Lagrangian representation, and a clipped-affine optimizer for sharp average-case bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The vector support function remains a linear objective under the same quadratic budget but gains regime-coupled normalization and consistency constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Efficient estimation and confidence intervals for longitudinal marginal-structural-model sensitivity-bound functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the common-law vector support function is identified, its sequential influence-function machinery is the nearest route to inference for contrasts and exposed faces of the joint set.

literature_map:
Tan (2006, JASA) supplies the propensity-score distributional formulation underlying the marginal sensitivity model.
Zhao, Small & Bhattacharya (2019, JRSSB) optimize empirical IPW bounds by linear-fractional programming and percentile bootstrap, but later work notes omitted marginalization constraints.
Dorn & Guo (2023, JASA; arXiv:2102.04543) impose quantile balance to obtain asymptotically sharp worst-case MSM bounds.
Dorn, Guo & Kallus (2025, JASA; arXiv:2112.11449) connect sharp MSM bounds to distributionally robust optimization and derive doubly-sharp/doubly-valid inference.
Yadlowsky et al. (2022, Annals of Statistics) derive conditional and average treatment-effect bounds under a Rosenbaum-style confounding model by empirical loss minimization.
Bonvini & Kennedy (2022, JASA; arXiv:1912.02793) use the proportion of confounded units, sharp bounds, flexible estimators, and a scalar robustness summary.
Bonvini, Kennedy, Ventura & Wasserman (2022; arXiv:2210.04681) allow time-varying treatment in marginal structural sensitivity models and derive efficient estimators and confidence intervals, but Tan notes that related propensity formulations omit inherent normalization constraints.
Tan (2024, JRSSB; arXiv:2209.11383) develops calibrated, model-assisted estimation and confidence intervals for relaxed cross-sectional MSM bounds.
Tan (2025, Biometrika; arXiv:2308.15725) gives the closest sequential full-law analysis: range-bounded sensitivity ratios, convex sharp/conservative population bounds, and attainment, while explicitly leaving computation and sample inference open.
Zhang & Zhao (2026, Biometrika; arXiv:2211.04697) replace worst-case caps by a global second moment of the propensity ratio, derive sharp clipped-affine bounds, EIF one-step estimators, and multiplier bands; their discussion explicitly calls longitudinal extension future work.
Masten & Poirier (2020, Quantitative Economics; arXiv:1705.04765) formulate breakdown frontiers and uniform lower bands, with nonregular directional-differentiability issues.
Masten, Poirier & Zhang (2024, JBES; arXiv:2012.15716) give bound-function bands uniform over a scalar unconfoundedness relaxation, but only in a one-period treatment model.
Fang & Santos (2019, Review of Economic Studies; arXiv:1404.3763) show why the standard bootstrap fails for merely directionally differentiable maps and provide derivative-aware resampling.
Ren, Telschow & Schwartzman (2024, JRSS-C; arXiv:2210.03933) show that simultaneous bands can be inverted into inner/outer inverse-set confidence regions without a unique transversal crossing.
The live seam is sequential compatible sharpness from Tan plus average-case quadratic budgets and band machinery from Zhang–Zhao; the searches found no existing paper proving their combination, its two-price dual, its uniform cross-fitted endpoint process, or full-ray inversion.
